timing: Authored before core freeze and before any candidate access or image call.
authority: Strict local scene tests of agent-owned staging, separate from requester meaning or native admission.
classification: PASS: every stated component visible together
FAIL: visible contradiction or missing visible component
UNOBSERVABLE: image evidence too small, occluded or ambiguous; never counts as pass

gates.criterion: The woman reads as a working music idol through at least three connected visible cues among stage-style outfit, cheek ear microphone, dressing-room mirror/tour objects, and performer-linked album/emblem/poster; attractive portrait alone fails.
A physical tablet screen clearly contains a remote fan, who holds a performer-linked album and shows a farewell palm; the screen is not merely a portrait or reflection.
The performer looks toward the displayed fan with a gently lowered chin/small softened smile and returns a raised-palm wave toward that screen in the same frame.
Performer, physical device boundary, remote fan face, album and the two distinct responding palms are spatially readable together; no fusion of screen and room.
The screen visibly carries 00:08 or an equally unambiguous eight-second remaining indicator; richer imagined last-seconds story is not established without visible timing.
The performer visibly retains the reference's short dark bob, wispy bangs and broadly corresponding face/eye/lip proportions at reviewable scale, without claiming identity.

Performer's left forearm is naturally supported and right wave connects plausibly to her bent elbow; remote fan holds album with one hand and raises the other; visible hands do not fuse with device edges.
A shared documentary frame carries an intimate closing interaction, with subject presence and readable device action; screen brightness or props do not overwhelm the face.

controls_impression_review: Describe actual pixels without intensity labels first, then compare sensual1/fetish0/surreal0/creativity1 intent. User preference remains pending.
